title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART stands in for Marco Polo — Richard died in 1199, seventy years before the journey, and is an English crusader king with no connection to the Polos; the engine offers generic merchants, villagers, or trade carts that would have been unobjectionable
BERSERK (a Scandinavian Viking unit, and by 1271 a long-obsolete one) placed in the Central Asian oasis force
CAVALIER, KNIGHT x5, CROSSBOWMAN x5, MILITIA x5, PIKEMAN x6 — a full Western European feudal battle line escorting what was actually a party of three Venetian merchants with a handful of servants
PAVILION_A / TENT_A / TENT_B (Western/Mediterranean camp architecture) used for the caravan on the Silk Road where the engine's yurts or Middle Eastern buildings were available
No trade carts, camels-as-pack-animals, or caravan objects despite the brief's claim that 'the caravan's pack animals must survive' — the four CAMEL_RIDERs are combat cavalry, not baggage
Niccolo Polo is named in dialogue but exists only as an unnamed VILLAGER_MALE, if at all
